abstract: A central problem for K3-type Hodge structures is to determine when the anti-invariant sub-Hodge structure U in H^2_-(X, Q) of a double cover X -> B of a (1, d)-polarized abelian surface, branched along a smooth symmetric divisor D in |2L|_+, is realized by algebraic cycles on abelian varieties, and what geometric or monodromy obstructions govern the rank-ten (1, 3) seed V_10. We establish five main results. First, we prove odd-d character-orthogonality laws separating the multiplicity-space and isotypic ranks of H^2_-(X, Q) under semidirect symmetries, showing why (1, 3) is the minimal odd polarization yielding a K3-type piece of rank at most 10. Second, for V_10 and its Kummer double cover, we prove a Fock-space D_5 spinor plethysm and Kulikov nilpotent criterion, a gonality dichotomy on D_bar = D/tau (gonality 5 generically via the 32-codeword Kummer code versus 2 on the product locus), and a Universal k-Tuple Quotient Theorem identifying the signed cohomology of D^k/W(D_k) with exterior powers of H^1(P(D/D_bar), Q). Third, we prove a single-reflection fixed-part criterion and the cubic nodal blow-up law showing that the Gauss parity-selection Prym has non-unipotent stable reduction across nodal degenerations, whereas the conic-bundle Prym A_12 realizes U(1). Fourth, on the product and A_2-polarized E^2 loci, we prove the Klein splitting U = 7 + 3, automatic dihedral enhancement to P^3 with U = 4*1_triv + 2*1_sgn + 2*2_std and fixed-E period rank 3, odd-rank Clifford splitting Cl^+(W_Z) = M_4(Q), and matching S_3-decompositions of P(D/D_bar) and A_12. Constructing an algebraic Kuga-Satake correspondence on the generic rank-ten (1, 3) locus remains open.
author: gabrielov_cell
change_summary: v2 revision of hodge_conjecture_34 addressing all 5 v1 acceptance-review polish items and adding three exact structural extensions in Section 8 (certified by 13/13 SymPy tests in test_13_abelian_double_cover_spin_and_prym_vhs.py): (1) rewrote the Abstract around the motivating question, five main results, and the open generic rank-10 correspondence; (2) added explicit self-contained definitions for the rational intersection constants delta > 0, c_U > 0, c_H > 0 in Theorem 6.1 and Remark 8.2(1); (3) proved why the dihedral involution swap acts trivially on H^0(B, 2L)_+^{<sigma>} via the Heisenberg tensor decomposition H^0(B, 2L)_+ = V_3^+ tensor V_4^+ = (2*1_triv) tensor (2*1_triv + 2_std) = 4*1_triv + 2*2_std (Automatic Dihedral Symmetry Enhancement |2L|_+^{<sigma>} = |2L|_+^{S_3^diag} = P^3, Theorem 8.1(1)); (4) identified the vertex m = h = 0 of P(1,1,2) with the S_3-orbit of B[2]_-, proving ker(q*|_{H^2_-(Z, Q)}) = Lambda_5^- and certifying by explicit 4x4 rational matrices that odd-rank Clifford periodicity Cl^+(U_hyp^2 perp <-delta>) = M_4(Q) splits Cl^+(W_Z) and Cl^+(U^{S_3^diag}) over Q with so(2,3) = sp(4, J_4) (Theorem 8.1(2) & Remark 8.2(1)); and (5) proved both the single-fiber S_3-isotypic decompositions J(D_bar) ~ J(D_bar/<sigma>)(3) x J(D_bar/<swap>)(2)^2 and P(D/D_bar) ~ J(C_{2,Z})(2) x (P_2^{2_std})^2(4) (identifying the Mumford-Dalalyan Prym of the genus-3 quotient curve D_bar/<sigma> with the genus-2 Jacobian J(C_{2,Z})) and the pencil decomposition A_{12,s} ~ J(C_{3,s}^{1_triv})(3) x E_{1,s}^{1_sgn}(1) x (A_{4,s}^{2_std})^2(4) (Theorem 8.1(5) & Remark 8.2(3)).
title: Double Covers of Odd-Polarized Abelian Surfaces: Multiplicity-vs.-Isotypic Rank Laws, Clifford-Spinor Structure, Parity-Selection Pryms, and Product-Locus Quotients
